themes.mechanism: Two full token sets under :root[data-theme="light"] (also the :root default) and :root[data-theme="dark"], same custom-property names. Frontmatter keys ending in -dark are the dark values of the same CSS variable.
themes.toggle: Light / Dark / System segmented radio group in the rail foot (lucide Sun, Moon, Monitor).
themes.boot: Inline script in index.html reads the key and sets data-theme and color-scheme before first paint; System follows prefers-color-scheme live.

headline.purpose: One page title in the panel head. 650 weight, text-wrap: balance.

title.purpose: Section headings in the setup wizard.

settings-title.purpose: Settings section headings and component names on Versions.

row-name.purpose: Service and project names in lists.

body.purpose: Running copy. Tabular figures on body. Ledes in text-2, max 64ch.

body-ui.purpose: Button labels, page summary, readable log, update notice title, banners.

section-title.purpose: Services and Log labels above their lists, text-2.

body-sm.purpose: Notices, Settings ledes, wizard option rows.

meta.purpose: Role lines, small-button labels, update notice text.

label.purpose: Hints, toggle segments, log mode buttons.

nav-group.purpose: Uppercase rail groupings (Workspace, App) only; never above headings.

mono-data.purpose: Versions, ports, uptimes, paths, raw log.

shadows.name: selected-lift
shadows.purpose: Current nav item and wizard step, active theme segment, active log mode.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Soft lift; alone on the terminal's selected tab and the update notice.

shadows.name: btn-edge
shadows.purpose: Default and small buttons; removed on press and when disabled.

shadows.name: status-halo
shadows.purpose: Running dot and the Settings update-ready dot.

shadows.name: ring
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on every :focus-visible, replacing outline.

motion.name: page-enter
motion.purpose: One entrance per page body; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: notice-in
motion.purpose: Update notice entrance; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: rail-collapse
motion.purpose: Rail collapse; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover and focus changes on controls and rows.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Status pill and install spinners; slowed under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: content-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Services rows fold port and uptime into the role line; grid 20px / 1fr / 116px / 150px.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Tighter head and section rhythm; log minimum 140px.

breakpoints.name: viewport-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Browser preview only: rail becomes a top bar, nav hidden, 16px gutters.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single next action of a view (Start all, Update now, Continue); blue face with an edge light, presses down 1px.

narrative.overview:
A Windows-native local stack manager built to the category standard of Laravel Herd and Docker Desktop. The window is one cool, tinted ground shared by the rail and the window edge; on it floats a single rounded work surface, lifted by a soft shadow and a hairline. Inside that surface, content reads as lists and sections separated by space and hairlines, never as a grid of boxed cards. Every number lines up, every state is honest, and nothing decorative stands in for clarity.

Colour is spent on meaning only. One confident blue marks the current place, focus, selection, the next action and the one "update ready" dot; green, amber and red appear only for running, needs attention and failed, always as small tinted pills, dots or boxes. Everything else is cool neutral greys arranged as tonal layers, with no surface at pure white so long sessions stay easy on the eyes. Buttons carry a faint edge light and a 1px drop so they read as pressable. Versions, ports and paths speak in a monospace voice; all figures are tabular; icons come from one line-icon library.

Both themes are first-class. Light and dark are full token sets under the same names, switched by `data-theme` on the root, chosen with a Light / Dark / System toggle stored as `nexdb.theme` and applied before first paint.
keyCharacteristics: Shared ground: window and rail are one colour; the rail has no border and no panel of its own.
One floating work surface (12px radius, panel shadow, hairline) holding the page; everything inside it is flat.
Lists, not cards: one bordered list per group, rows divided by hairlines; settings sections divided by a hairline, not boxed.
Status as small tinted pills with a dot; neutral states stay grey.
Buttons with depth tokens (`--btn-bg`, `--btn-edge`, `--btn-primary-edge`) that press down 1px.
Segoe UI Variable with tabular figures; Cascadia Mono for versions, ports and paths.
Lucide line icons only; no glyph characters as icons; no eyebrow labels above headings.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "this is where you are, this is chosen, this has focus, or this is your next action." It never decorates, never labels a category and never marks a recommendation.

rules.name: The Earned Status Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only when something is running, needs attention or has failed. Stopped, Starting and Not running are neutral grey pills.

rules.name: The Off-White Rule
rules.body: No surface is pure white. The brightest material is the button face, one step above the work surface; white is reserved for text on blue.

rules.name: The Shared Ground Rule
rules.body: The rail sits on the window ground with no fill and no border of its own; only the work surface is a separate material.

rules.name: The Inverted Recommendation Rule
rules.body: "Recommended" is a neutral inverted tag (`text` background, `surface` text) so it stands out without borrowing blue or green.

rules.name: The Data Voice Rule
rules.body: Versions, ports, uptimes and filesystem paths are always set in the mono family; prose never is.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body so every count, port and uptime aligns.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Page and section headings stand alone. There is no small label, kicker or category line above a title. The uppercase nav-group style belongs to the rail's navigation and is not used above headings.

rules.name: The One Floating Surface Rule
rules.body: Only the work surface floats. Lists, sections, banners and boxes inside it carry a hairline or a tint, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Pressable Rule
rules.body: Buttons have an edge light and a 1px drop; on press they move down 1px and lose the shadow; disabled and quiet buttons are flat.

dos: Do keep the window and rail on one shared ground, and float only the work surface (12px radius, `--shadow-panel`, hairline, 8px margin).
Do group things as one bordered list with hairline-divided rows (10px radius), and divide Settings sections with a hairline, not a box.
Do show status as a tinted capsule pill with a dot; keep Stopped, Starting and Not running grey.
Do reserve blue (`accent`) for the current place, selection, focus, the single primary action and the update-ready dot.
Do give default buttons `--btn-bg` and `--btn-edge`, primaries `--btn-primary-edge`, and a 1px press.
Do step radii down as elements nest: 12, 10, 8, 7, 6.
Do set versions, ports, uptimes and paths in Cascadia Mono, and keep tabular figures on.
Do use lucide line icons (12-18px) for every icon, bare, with a text label on row actions.
Do dock app-level notices in the rail foot so they never cover the work.
Do give an empty area a centred plain-language note and the one action that fills it.
Do fold secondary columns into the line under the name when the content is narrower than 760px.
Do define every colour for both themes under the same token name.
donts: Don't use pure white for any surface; white is only for text on blue.
Don't add shadows to lists, banners or sections inside the work surface.
Don't lay out a grid of boxed cards, one per thing, or put icons on tinted tiles.
Don't put eyebrow or kicker labels above page or section headings.
Don't use text glyphs (check marks, arrows, bullets, stars) as icons.
Don't use opacity to show a disabled control.
Don't colour recommendations, categories or neutral facts with blue or a status hue.
Don't set prose in the mono family.
